Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Setup 2 Gameplay 3 End of the Game 4 Character Powers Setup One player plays as the nurse. The other plays as Capulet. Place the board between both players. The nurse places the 6 characters anywhere on the board, but each space can only have one character. Then, she chooses 2 characters to be Romeo and Juliet, disguised. They are placed down secretly. The other characters are returned to the box. Take the 15 pair tiles and place them next to the board. They are the possible combinations of Romeo and Juliet. Gameplay On each round Capulet moves first. The players take turns to move an active character onto any empty space with their abilities. Then they flip it to the passive side. After all characters are moved, the nurse reports whether the lovers are in the same area. There are two areas on the board: the perimeter and the center. Capulet then eliminates all impossible pairs. After each round, all characters are flipped back to active. End of the Game If Capulet eliminates pairs such that only one possible pair is left, he finds the lovers and wins. Otherwise, if seven rounds have passed and at least two pairs are left, the nurse successfully hid the lovers for seven days and wins. Character Powers Princess: She can move any number of squares in any direction. Prince: He can move one square in any direction. Noble: He can move any number of squares orthodiagonally. Servant: He can move one square orthodiagonally. Bishop: He can move any number of squares diagonally. Friar: He can jump to the first empty space behind a character. He cannot jump in a direction with no characters. All characters except the friar cannot jump. [Rating: 2.1/10] Bár a fejtágítást megkaptam youtube-on, hogy ez kicsit sem hasonlít MrJack-re kipróbáltam a társasjáték ünnepen, és a grafika tagadhatatlanul gyönyörű, én még is azt érzem, hogy ez a Mr Jack egy visszabutított változata. Ott is lényeg, a kizáráshoz, hogy a megfelelő helyre vidd a karaktereket. Nagyon nem mindegy, hogy fényben vannak e vagy sem. Itt blokkolni tudod a másik útját, kisebb a pálya  és sakozosabb lépések vannak benne, de nekem tól száraz. Persze kinek a pap, kinek a papné. Ettől másnak tetszhet de nálam ez nagyon nem hozta az elvárásokat :/

[Rating: 3/10] 2 Player abstract deduction game that is really lacking in the gameplay. Playing as the Nurse seems very difficult and the first few turns are unimportant. Unfortunately, I can't see playing this anymore.

[Rating: 4/10] Not my type of game - deduction mingled with chess. But pretty, and possibly a good quick game for those that are into it.

[Rating: 4/10] The deduction element of Verona Twist is fine, but what I really didn’t care for is the mechanism utilized to achieve that.  It just reminds me too much of chess where to do well I would have to look several moves ahead, calculating the possibilities of my opponent’s actions in response to mine.  Honestly, it’s too much effort for such an inconsequential game, and it is 7 rounds too long.

[Rating: 4/10] Mr. Jack but simpler. Seems very unbalanced from a first glance, though. Not sure how the nurse can win.

[Rating: 4.5/10] Looked like a really cool deduction game, but after a few plays, it seema highly unbalanced to me. It's way to easy to win as Capulet.

[Rating: 5/10] Ok game. Was highly anticipated for me and really liked the idea. But for me i didn't really work in two ways.   - The nurse was never near winning.  - The first two rounds wasn't so interesting, then it became really exiting a few moves but it always ended after maximum five out of seven rounds.  It is absolutely possible that it becomes better after for example ten more plays. But I didn't find it interesting enough to spend that time.

[Rating: 5/10] Quick deduction game somewhat similar to Mr Jack Pocket.  Seems tough to play the nurse.
